name: relation-dictionary
direction_note: Every relation reads SUBJECT -> OBJECT in the order stated by `covers`. The upstream registry defines the edge NAMES only and says nothing about argument order, so this file supplies it; that is a gap in the ratified contract rather than a disagreement with it, and it is part of what the additions owe upstream. `inverse_synonyms` are surface forms that state the SAME relation with the arguments the other way round: a filer matching one of those must SWAP the two ends. Keeping them in their own field is what stops a reversed phrasing from resolving confidently to a false edge — a collision fails to resolve and is visible, a reversal succeeds and is not.
attribute_boundary: A one-place fact about a person is an ATTRIBUTE and belongs to attribute-dictionary.json, not here. That includes family: relationship.* holds the user's family facts, so no family relation appears in this file. A family fact between two OTHER named people is homeless in both artifacts — recorded in `refused` rather than left to be rediscovered.

relations.covers: type or category assertion; shares its surface form with HAS_OCCUPATION and the OBJECT decides — a category takes IS_A, a job role takes HAS_OCCUPATION
a person to a work item they are working on
a requirement one thing has of another
a preference of one named thing over another
a standing prohibition
current use of a thing by a person or system; the "built with X" family is deliberately absent because it does not decide between this and IMPLEMENTED_IN
a structural dependency
causation between two events or things
a defect and what repaired it
a decision taken about a thing
the REPLACEMENT and the thing it replaces, in that order
a process or artifact and the rule that governs it
ownership of a thing by a person or group
membership of a person in a group or organization
a thing and where it is
a person and a skill they hold
a person and a topic they follow
a person and an account or handle they hold
a person and their role or job title; shares its surface form with IS_A and the OBJECT decides — a job role takes HAS_OCCUPATION, a category takes IS_A
a thing and a MEASURED QUANTITY of it; the object must be a number with a unit, which is why the broad verb "handles" is deliberately absent
a person and their employer, present or past
a person and an event or institution they attended; the vague "was at" is deliberately absent because it does not decide between this and LOCATED_AT
a person and the person they report to; direction is subordinate to manager
two people working together as peers, with no hierarchy asserted; the same sentence usually ALSO yields WORKS_ON for each of them, which is two facts rather than a conflict
a person and the person, book or source they learned something from, LEARNER first

a thing that was used or attempted and is deliberately no longer used; the negative counterpart of USES, and NOT the same as FORBIDS, which is a rule rather than a history. A sentence that also names the choice yields DECIDED as well — two facts, not a conflict
a work item and what is currently blocking it; a live state, unlike DEPENDS_ON which is structural and permanent

a system and the language or platform it is written in; distinct from USES, which loses that the thing IS that language. The "built with / built in" family is deliberately absent from BOTH — one word apart for two different relations is not a cue a filer can use
a behaviour or defect and the condition it appears under; a condition, NOT a cause — CAUSED asserts something did produce it
an artifact and another artifact it references; the vague "builds on" is deliberately absent because it does not decide between this and DEPENDS_ON

a person or system and the artifact they made, MAKER first; authorship is what OWNED_BY and WORKS_ON both fail to express — owning a thing is not having made it, and working on a thing is not having finished it

refused.why: a schedule is an attribute of the event, not a two-place relation to an entity; a weekday is not a thing the graph holds
one supporting sentence, and the claim is close enough to IS_A or DEPENDS_ON that no filer could choose reliably
a three-place fact; this vocabulary is two-place by construction and splitting it invents two relations neither of which is what was said

family facts about the USER live in the attribute dictionary under relationship.*, so no family relation belongs in this file; a family fact between two OTHER named people is genuinely homeless and accepted as lost, because a memory system for one user rarely needs the family tree of third parties
a function signature detail; it is readable from the record text, and admitting it invites one relation per language construct

DEFERRED, NOT SETTLED — a real gap for the student user type, but it needs its negative twin CONTRADICTS or it records only agreement, and a directional evidence pair is an owner call rather than a filing-test call. Raised 2026-08-17; nothing may treat this as closed without a ruling
